For a while, many people weren't sure whether clamshell or book-style would be the future of foldable smartphones, but for now, it looks like book-style folding has already won.

Samsung's 8th generation foldable phone uses this design, the upcoming iPhone Ultra is also expected to adopt it, and even leaked images of the Xiaomi 18 Fold follow this trend...

There are two body designs for foldable smartphones, commonly referred to as clamshell and book-style.

The clamshell design essentially folds a traditional smartphone in half into a thicker but half-height device, maintaining a normal-sized screen while being more pocket-friendly. The Motorola Razr is one example, paying homage to a design first pioneered by the company back in 2004.

The book-style design is increasingly being called "book-style" — the reason is obvious: the body itself is closer to square, and when unfolded it's like a small tablet similar to an iPad mini. This is exactly the design Apple plans to unveil next month.

Samsung's Galaxy Z Fold series popularized this design, with the 8th generation model having just debuted last month.

Xiaomi is now also preparing to join the fray with its 18 Fold, whose camera module design bears some resemblance to the rumored look of the iPhone Ultra. Weibo user Peter shared two photos (above), speculating this is likely an engineering sample rather than the final production model.

Our sister site 9to5Google mentioned that this deep cherry color appears to reference one of the rumored color options for the iPhone 18 Pro.
